subject.title: [Security]: Custom clientFactory proxy pools bypass SSRF allowedHostnames allowlist

question: Should OpenClaw treat custom Undici proxy `clientFactory` as a trusted escape hatch, or should guarded/SDK proxy helpers reject or wrap it to preserve SSRF and pinned-dispatcher guarantees?
rationale: This is a core network security boundary decision: a mechanical fix could harden the helper, but it may also change an exported plugin SDK proxy contract and break intentional custom transports.

options.title: Harden guarded proxy helpers
options.body: Reject or wrap custom `clientFactory` where OpenClaw promises SSRF/pinned-dispatcher behavior, and add tests for preserved lookup and allowlist enforcement.

options.title: Document trusted escape hatch
options.body: Keep custom factories as trusted code, but document that callers bypass OpenClaw's managed proxy factory guarantees and must enforce their own network policy.

options.title: Narrow SDK exposure
options.body: Move low-level proxy factory customization out of the supported plugin SDK surface or gate it behind a safer specialized helper.

recommendation.title: Harden guarded proxy helpers
recommendation.body: Reject or wrap custom `clientFactory` where OpenClaw promises SSRF/pinned-dispatcher behavior, and add tests for preserved lookup and allowlist enforcement.
